column1: # CI's seconds per shell suite, read by tests/lib/fast-tier.py's check (j), which holds the Slow tier (ADR 0084 d3) to
# them: a suite at or over SLOW_JOIN (180 s) must be on a `SLOW` line of tests/fast-tier.map, and a SLOW suite under
# SLOW_LEAVE (150 s) must leave it; between the two either is fine, so a suite near the cutoff does not flap as the
# medians drift. Its docstring holds the format and the rules. Nothing else reads it: the selection reads the SLOW
# Source: the per-suite `<label>: ok (<N>s)` and `<label>: FAILED (<N>s)` lines of GitHub's macos-latest jobs from
# 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-15 (322 jobs on both runners, 161 on macOS: the 2026-11-16 suite audit's jobs-parsed.json,
# docs/audits/test-suite-audit-2026-11-16.md), every macOS job that printed the line, whatever its conclusion. Each
# value is that suite's median. macOS because it is the slowest runner, so the medians spread most at the cutoff, and
# master's full-suite.yml keeps running macOS shards that print the same lines. The merge-task self-tests and node
# files have no row (node prints no per-file time), so they are never SLOW by this file.
# Regenerate: from a week's macOS job logs (master's full-suite.yml macOS shards; the PR check runs on ubuntu alone
# since 2026-11-16, ADR 0084 d3), take each shell suite's median of those lines, and rewrite this file whole, one
# `<seconds><TAB><suite>` row per collected shell suite. A refresh that moves a suite across the cutoff fails check (j)
# until the same PR edits its SLOW line.
# The four leg rows (tests/leg.test.sh and its parts leg-land, leg-rank, leg-security, split from it by p54-9) are
# their own, until the next regenerate: each is that suite's median of the same lines in master's full-suite.yml macOS
# shards since the split, 2026-11-16T15:00Z to 2026-11-19 (27 runs, 94 macOS jobs with a runner, every attempt's; a job
# GitHub never gave a runner prints no line): leg.test.sh over 24 lines, leg-land 23, leg-rank 21, leg-security 23.
